questions.question:
D1 — Final Approval Gate: approve the reviewed plan?
Project/branch/task: main · /autoplan on "Plan: User Dashboard Page" (all four review phases complete, plan amended on disk).
ELI10: Four reviews ran and made 117 routine calls for you; four are matters of taste (T1 aggregate endpoint, T2 keep the confirmation modal, T3 build the dashboard rather than a cheaper spike first, T4 row caps). Approving locks the amended plan and writes the review logs so /ship recognizes it. Overriding lets you flip any taste call before implementation starts.
Stakes if we pick wrong: approving a taste call you disagree with means rework mid-implementation; rejecting throws away 121 logged decisions and four reviews.
Recommendation: A because every blocking finding is resolved, no premise was clearly wrong, and the four taste calls follow your stated direction where you gave one.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Approve as-is (recommended)
  ✅ Plan is fully amended with accepted obligations for all four phases and 34 build-ready tasks
  ✅ Review logs get written now so /ship's dashboard shows CEO, Design, DX, and Eng as reviewed
  ❌ The modal (T2) stays even though two independent subagents recommend cutting it
B) Approve with overrides on taste decisions
  ✅ You pick T1-T4 explicitly; I apply the changes to the plan and re-run Eng on the amended plan
  ✅ Keeps every other decision and artifact intact
  ❌ Costs one more Eng pass (~2 min of pipeline time) before the gate re-presents
C) Interrogate a decision first
  ✅ Ask about any of the 121 decisions, tasks, or superseded items before committing
  ✅ No plan changes until you say so
  ❌ Adds a round trip before approval
D) Revise the plan or start over
  ✅ Change scope or architecture and re-run the affected phases (max 3 cycles), or reject and restart
  ✅ The restore point holds the original plan bytes for a clean re-run
  ❌ Re-running phases repeats the subagent passes and their wall-clock time
Net: A ships the reviewed plan now; B is the right pick if you want the modal cut or three fetches instead of the aggregate.
